labels.label: def:almost_everywhere_atlas_topological
questions: 'Supported by some portly subset' read as 'the support is portly'; equivalent to 'the support contains a portly subset' (isAEAtlas_iff_exists_isPortly) since supports are open. The unlabelled notions of l.406 (complete, completion, thinner) are formalized with their two claims (completion is a complete (G,X)-atlas; completion of a thinner atlas is thinner).

labels.label: lem:GX_atlas_union

hypotheses.note: not used: chart sources are locally connected through X
X locally connected + Hausdorff, rigid action, by homeomorphisms

findings: l.412: for an empty family the union is the empty atlas, whose support ∅ is not portly in a nonempty N, so the lemma needs K nonempty (GX.not_isAEAtlas_iUnion_empty). Harmless for its only use, cor:maximal_atlas, where the family contains A.

labels.label: cor:maximal_atlas
questions: The maximum is proved both for the preorder <= (it is >= every B >= A) and for inclusion (IsGreatest), which makes it unique; <= is shown reflexive and transitive. maximalAEAtlas_eq_of_aeLe: A <= B gives the same maximum.

labels.label: def:singular_manifold_locally_connected

hypotheses.paper: M locally connected Hausdorff second countable
hypotheses.note: as instance arguments where used; all three bundled in SingGXCat

questions: The class SingularGXStructure carries only the maximal a.e. atlas (DEC-25); the topological hypotheses are separate instances, each theorem asking for those it uses.

labels.label: def:morphism
questions: 'f restricted to U, V is a (G,X)-morphism' is read subtype-free as IsRegularOn (continuous on U, f(U) ⊆ Reg N, in charts of A at x and of B at f x locally an element of G), the WP-24c reading of a (G,X)-morphism; chart independence IsRegularOn.of_exists. isAEMorphismOf_iff: V may always be taken to be Reg(N).

labels.label: rem:composition_morphisms_morphisms_category

hypotheses.note: the source of the composite: the trace of the preimage of a portly set under a map that is a local homeomorphism on a portly set is portly

questions: The paper's assertion that isomorphisms are exactly the homeomorphisms which are a.e. morphisms needs the inverse to be an a.e. morphism; proved (IsAEMorphismOf.symm_of_homeomorph, via lem:GX_sing_homeo_reg and the atlas transport of rem:consequence).

labels.label: rem:morphisms_analytical_two_equal
findings: l.491: 'if two [a.e. (G,X)-morphisms] are equal on an open set, they are equal everywhere' is false as written: (1) the open set must be nonempty (id and the translation by 1 on R agree on ∅, GX.analytic_counterexample_empty); (2) M must be connected, which def:singular_manifold_locally_connected does not ask (on R ⊕ R with the translations, id and the map translating the second copy agree on the first copy, GX.analytic_counterexample_disconnected). Both counterexamples satisfy every hypothesis of the paper (locally connected, Hausdorff, second countable, empty singular locus).

labels.label: prop:GX_sing_morph_local

hypotheses.note: source locally connected, target an a.e. atlas; source atlas arbitrary

questions: The paper does not define the a.e. structure induced on an open (or portly) subset W, nor 'locally an a.e. morphism'. Read: 'f|W is an a.e. morphism' = some U ⊆ W, portly in W (Portly's subtype convention), on which f induces a (G,X)-morphism into Reg N (IsAEMorphismOn); 'locally' = every point has an open W with f|W an a.e. morphism. Under this reading all three equivalences are proved.

hypotheses.note: a.e. atlases suffice (no maximality, no topological hypothesis on M, N)

labels.label: rem:though_may_tempted_include
questions: Informal remark. Formalized content: for p ≠ 1, 0 ∉ Reg(z ↦ z^p) for every pair of a.e. atlases on C (no hypothesis), hence (lem:regf1) z ↦ z^p is an a.e. morphism for no a.e. structures regular at 0 and at 0^p. The sentence 'there is no simple definition of Riemann surfaces as (G,X)-manifolds' is not formalized.

labels.label: lem:aepullback

hypotheses.paper: f continuous, a.e. a local homeomorphism
hypotheses.note: IsAELocalHomeomorph read from the proof's first line

findings: l.545: 'there exists a unique a.e. (G,X)-structure' — an a.e. structure is an a.e. atlas (def:structure_topological_space_atlas, l.471), and uniqueness fails among all of them (two different a.e. atlases on R make id an a.e. morphism, GX.aePullback_counterexample_nonmaximal); the proof's appeal to maximality shows uniqueness is meant among maximal ones, which is what is proved.
questions: 'f is a.e. a local homeomorphism' is undefined; read from the proof: portly O ⊆ M and P ⊆ Reg(N) with f(O) ⊆ P and f a local homeomorphism on O.

labels.label: def:notations_lemma_lem_aepullback
questions: aePullback G B f is the unique maximal structure when one exists and ∅ (junk) otherwise.

labels.label: cor:locally_connected_hausdorff_topological

hypotheses.paper: (implicit) g, f a.e. local homeomorphisms into Reg(N), Reg(g^*A)
hypotheses.note: added: without them the pullbacks f^*g^*A, (g∘f)^*A are not defined by lem:aepullback

hypotheses.paper: A an a.e. structure on N

findings: l.558: the corollary does not say that g and f are almost everywhere local homeomorphisms (into Reg N and into Reg of g^*A), without which g^*A and f^*g^*A are undefined; those hypotheses are added.

labels.label: lem:GX_sing_homeo_reg

hypotheses.note: an a.e. atlas suffices; N's atlas maximal is used

questions: 'f is a local homeomorphism around x' read as IsLocalHomeomorphOn f {x}. The proof is not the paper's (which goes through f^*B = A): the chart e ∘ h⁻¹ built from a local inverse h is compatible with B, so belongs to B by maximality (mem_of_compatible).

labels.label: cor:morphisms_also_local_homemorphism
questions: 'Preserves both regular and singular loci' read (strongly) as f⁻¹(Reg N) = Reg M and f⁻¹(Sing N) = Sing M; needs both atlases maximal.

labels.label: rem:consequence_isomorphism_singular_manifolds
questions: Proved: f^*B = A, and concretely e ∈ A ↔ e ∘ f⁻¹ ∈ B. The final sentence ('an isomorphism in every natural ways') is informal and not formalized.

kb_proposals: Maximal a.e. atlases: IsMaximalAEAtlas.mem_of_compatible (a chart locally G-compatible with every chart of A is in A) is the workhorse — completeness, lem:GX_sing_homeo_reg, the cor and the iso remark all reduce to it; prove membership by building the chart and checking local compatibility.

Rigidity on any preconnected subset of a chart source (exists_smul_eq_on_of_isPreconnected, F arbitrary, S need not be open) plus Set.EqOn.of_subset_closure over a portly set is the 'locally constant g on the portly trace, then density' step of lem:GX_atlas_union and lem:regf1.

Singular-manifold notions are stated for explicit atlases (IsAEMorphismOf G A B f, regLocusOf G A B f) with class-level wrappers over SingularGXStructure; the explicit form is what the pullback (structure on M varies) needs.

A (G,X)-manifold is a singular one with empty Sing: isMaximalAEAtlas_maximalAtlas and isAEMorphismOf_maximalAtlas_iff; cheap counterexamples on ℝ and ℝ ⊕ ℝ with Multiplicative ℝ (hasGroupoid_sum_translation) come from this bridge.
